prompt:
Build a coupled vehicle thermal-management model containing finite thermal storage for cabin air, cabin interior mass, a generic power-electronics/e-drive component, and a liquid coolant loop. Include ambient and solar heat transfer, cabin internal heat gain, component heat generation, a coolant pump and radiator path, cabin PTC heating, and one finite refrigerant system whose total cooling capacity is shared between a cabin evaporator and a coolant chiller.

Read ambient_temperature, solar_irradiance, cabin_internal_gain, component_heat_load, cabin_temperature_setpoint, component_temperature_limit, refrigerant_capacity, component_heat_step_fraction, heat_step_time, compressor_capacity_loss, and capacity_event_time from base-workspace variables. Their nominal values are 303.15 K, 450 W/m^2, 650 W, 3500 W, 295.15 K, 318.15 K, 10000 W, 0.35, 1200 s, 0.30, and 2100 s. They operate respectively over 258.15--313.15 K, 0--900 W/m^2, 0--1600 W, 1500--6500 W, 293.15--297.15 K, 313.15--323.15 K, 8000--14000 W, 0--0.60, 900--1800 s, 0--0.50, and 1500--2600 s. The component heat increase lasts 600 s. The refrigerant-capacity loss lasts 450 s.

The per-variable ranges do not define an unrestricted Cartesian product. Let Q_component_event = component_heat_load*(1+component_heat_step_fraction), Q_available_event = refrigerant_capacity*(1-compressor_capacity_loss), and Q_cabin_screen = cabin_internal_gain+4*solar_irradiance. Evaluation uses only joint tuples satisfying all of the following public admissibility conditions: component_temperature_limit-ambient_temperature >= 5 K; Q_available_event >= 0.75*Q_component_event; Q_available_event >= Q_cabin_screen+0.25*Q_component_event; and 8000 W+Q_cabin_screen >= 150 W/K*max(cabin_temperature_setpoint-ambient_temperature,0 K). These inequalities only exclude combinations that fail a basic energy and heat-rejection feasibility screen; they are not the score formula and do not prescribe the model topology or controller.

At every admissible evaluated operating point, regulate the actual cabin-air temperature to cabin_temperature_setpoint, keep the actual component temperature below component_temperature_limit, coordinate the two consumers of the shared refrigerant capacity, and recover after both temporary events. Coolant mass flow must not exceed 0.35 kg/s, PTC heat must not exceed 8000 W, and the active cooling system must have a physically plausible coefficient of performance between 1.5 and 6. Initialize all thermal states from an ambient soak.

Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named thermal_state, thermal_flow, actuator_state, and energy_state. thermal_state has 4 channels in this order: cabin air, cabin interior mass, cooled component, and coolant temperature, all in K. thermal_flow has 11 channels in this order: ambient-to-cabin, ambient-to-interior-mass, interior-mass-to-cabin, cabin gain, PTC-to-cabin, evaporator-from-cabin, component generation, component-to-coolant, chiller-from-coolant, radiator-to-ambient, and condenser-to-ambient heat flow, all in W. actuator_state has 12 channels in this order: compressor command (1), available cooling capacity (W), evaporator allocation (1), chiller allocation (1), coolant-pump command (1), coolant mass flow (kg/s), cabin-blower command (1), radiator bypass (1), compressor power (W), pump power (W), blower power (W), and PTC power (W). energy_state has 4 channels in this order: cumulative compressor, coolant-pump, cabin-blower, and PTC electrical energy, all in kWh. Positive ambient-to-cabin, ambient-to-interior-mass, interior-mass-to-cabin, component-to-coolant, radiator-to-ambient, and condenser-to-ambient heat follows the named source-to-destination direction. The other named heat transfers are nonnegative magnitudes in their named directions. Outputs must come from the causal thermal network and actual actuators rather than duplicated setpoints or precomputed traces.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XTHERM01.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
